source_text: Προδήλων οὖν ἡμῖν ὄντων τούτων, καὶ ἐγκεκυφότες εἰς τὰ βάθη τῆς θείας γνώσεως. πάντα τάξει ποιεῖν ὀφείλομεν, ὅσα ὁ δεσπότης ἐπιτελεῖν ἐκέλευσεν κατὰ καιροὺς τεταγμένους. τάς τε προσφορὰς καὶ λειτουργίας ἐπιτελεῖσθαι, καὶ οὐκ εἰκῆ ἢ ἀτάκτως ἐκέλευσεν γίνεσθαι, ἀλλ’ ὡρισμένοις καιροῖς καὶ ὥραις. ποῦ τε καὶ διὰ τίνων ἐπιτελεῖσθαι θέλει, αὐτὸς ὥρισεν τῇ ὑπερτάτῳ αὐτοῦ βουλήσει. ἵν’ ὁσίως πάντα γινόμενα ἐν εὐδοκήσει εὐπρόσδεκτα εἴη τῷ θελήματι αὐτοῦ. οἱ οὖν τοῖς προστεταγμένοις καιροῖς ποιοῦντες τὰς προσφορὰς αὐτῶν εὐπρόσδεκτοί τε καὶ μακάριοι: τοῖς γὰρ νομίμοις τοῦ δεσπότου ἀκολουθοῦντες οὐ διαμαρτάνουσιν. τῷ γὰρ ἀρχιερεῖ ἴδιαι λειτουργίαι δεδομέναι εἰσίν, καὶ τοῖς ἱερεῦσιν ἴδιος ὁ τόπος προστέτακται, καὶ Λευΐταις ἴδιαι διακονίαι ἐπίκεινται: ὁ λαϊκὸς ἄνθρωπος τοῖς λαῖκοῖς προστάγμασιν δέδεται.
pass_a_gloss: Being obvious to us that these things are so, and having been plunged into the depths of divine knowledge, we ought to do all things in order, as many things as the Master commanded to be done at appointed times. And the offerings and services are to be done, and He did not command them to be done randomly or disorderly, but at defined times and hours. Where and through whom He wishes them to be done, He Himself defined by His highest will, so that all things happening may be holy and acceptable in His good pleasure. Those, then, doing their offerings at the appointed times are acceptable and blessed: for following the lawful things of the Master, they do not sin. For the high priest, his own services have been given, and to the priests their own place has been appointed, and to the Levites their own ministries are assigned: the lay person is bound to the lay precepts.
pass_b_english: Since these truths are obvious to us and we have been plunged into the depths of divine knowledge, we must do everything in an orderly way — everything the Master commanded to be done at appointed times. He commanded that offerings and services be carried out, not haphazardly or in disorder, but at set times and hours. He himself determined by his supreme will where and through whom they should be done, so that everything done may be holy and acceptable to his good pleasure. Therefore those who present their offerings at the appointed times are acceptable and blessed, because by following the Master's lawful commands they do not sin. Distinct services have been assigned to the high priest, a specific place has been appointed for the priests, particular ministries are laid on the Levites, and the lay person is bound by the precepts for the laity.

review.notes: The translation accurately reflects the Greek text. Pass A and Pass B both correctly handle the nuances of the Greek, such as the distinction between the high priest, priests, Levites, and laity. The translation of 'οὐ διαμαρτάνουσιν' as 'they do not sin' (Pass A/B) or 'they do not murmur/complain' is a matter of interpretation, but 'do not sin' is a valid rendering of the sense in this context. The title 'Order in Worship' correctly captures the thought of the chapter.
